parsed.explanation: The dossier documents no trans-specific offence, police targeting, or violence against trans visitors. It also does not establish social acceptance or effective visitor-facing protections, so the evidence supports only a cautious, modestly reduced-risk assessment—not a claim of safety. The clearest traveler-relevant concern is reported border-crossing confusion when a trans man’s foreign ID conflicts with the territory’s records; the dossier gives no outcome such as denial of entry or detention, so this is a limited, uncertain exposure rather than a demonstrated severe restriction. The absence of local gender-marker recognition is principally a resident-facing gap and should not itself be treated as a visitor penalty. School bullying and an official’s 2018 referral statement are dated, resident-focused signals; the official later apologised. Same-sex relationship restrictions and protections framed around sexual orientation are climate signals, not direct trans-traveler rules. Thin evidence leaves important questions unresolved, rather than proving either safety or systematic danger.
